title: Paperwork and timing: KYC, nomination, cut-off, exit load, lock-in, TER
objectives: Explain KYC, FATCA/CRS and nomination, and why they come before investing.
Say how cut-off time, exit load and lock-in each affect a transaction.
body_md:
KYC (Know Your Customer) is a one-time identity and address verification recorded with a KYC Registration Agency; a FATCA/CRS declaration states tax residency. Nomination names who receives the investment if the investor dies. Cut-off time is the time by which a transaction (with money received) must reach the AMC to get that day's NAV: 3 pm for most funds, 1:30 pm for liquid and overnight funds. An exit load is a fee for redeeming early; a lock-in (ELSS: 3 years per instalment) blocks redemption entirely. TER is the yearly running cost, taken daily from the NAV and capped by SEBI.

| Term | Plain meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KYC (Know Your Customer) | One-time identity and address verification, recorded with a KYC Registration Agency | PAN, Aadhaar-based or in-person verification |
| FATCA / CRS declaration | Tax-residency declaration required for every investor | Asked at account opening |
| Nomination | Naming who receives the investment if the investor dies; more than one nominee can be named | Saves the family months of paperwork |
| Cut-off time | The time by which a transaction (with money received) must reach the AMC to get that day's NAV. 3 pm for most funds; earlier (1:30 pm) for liquid and overnight funds | Money received after cut-off gets the next day's NAV |
| Exit load | Fee charged if you redeem before a set period | Many equity funds charge 1% if redeemed within a year (check each scheme) |
| Lock-in | A period during which you cannot redeem at all | ELSS: 3 years for each SIP instalment separately |
| TER (Total Expense Ratio) | Annual cost of running the fund, taken daily from the NAV. SEBI caps it | TER 1.5% on ₹10 lakh ≈ ₹15,000 a year |
example: Money received after the 3 pm cut-off gets the next day's NAV — for purchases, what counts is when the AMC receives the money, not when the form was submitted.
say: For purchases, the NAV depends on when the AMC receives the money.
Exit load is a fee; a lock-in blocks exit entirely.
never: Exit load and lock-in mean the same thing.
Submitting a form before 3 pm guarantees that day's NAV, whatever time the money arrives.

check.q: The cut-off time for most equity funds is:
check.why: 3 pm. Liquid and overnight funds: 1:30 pm.

check.q: How do an exit load and a lock-in differ?
